qt: to the Commission Charles Goerens (Renew), Bernard Guetta (Renew), Fabienne Keller (Renew), Lukas Sieper (Renew), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew), Irena Joveva (Renew), Murielle Laurent (S&D), Jan-Christoph Oetjen (Renew), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew) Subject:

Since its beginnings in 2009, the European Website on Integration – which recently became the migrant integration hub – was the only source of information to monitor the 27 EU Member States’ almost daily updates on the same platform. It was also the Commission’s main tool for providing information and sharing the latest trends, news, best practices and initiatives to do with integration. With its content coming from a network of national correspondents, and its coordination taken care of by the Migration Policy Group for many years, the site became an important place to public actors and civil society. Over the past seven years, regular and rapid publication of content, supported in particular by civil society, has led to an exponential increase in visits to this platform. While the website has always been part of the Commission’s web infrastructure, recent changes to how it is managed – including the exclusion of civil society and national academic experts – seem to have slowed down the sharing of information. 1.
How will the Commission ensure best practices and information on integration continue to be shared within and between Member States?
What are the reasons for cutting back on the participatory model based on national correspondents?
What steps will be taken to ensure the continued existence of a responsive and accessible European platform dedicated to integration issues?
